root_cause.text: `hid_post_reset()` in `drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-core.c` allocated the HID report descriptor buffer with `GFP_KERNEL`, which can trigger reclaim/block I/O and deadlock while the USB reset path already holds the mutex for device/interface reset handling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `rdesc = kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, GFP_KERNEL);` to `GFP_NOIO`, and the CVE/commit message says `hid_pre_reset()` and `hid_post_reset()` run in block I/O error handling for devices with combined HID + storage/UAS components, so allocations there must not do block I/O because it can deadlock on the reset mutex.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a non-I/O memory allocation context when allocating the HID report descriptor after reset to avoid unsafe reclaim behavior.
intent_record.what: The allocation of `rdesc` in `hid_post_reset()` was changed from `kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, GFP_NOIO)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the allocation avoid direct reclaim and filesystem I/O while handling a USB HID post-reset path, reducing the risk of blocking on I/O-related memory pressure in this context.

candidates.rationale: This allocation uses GFP_KERNEL in the USB reset/post-reset path, which may sleep and invoke reclaim or block I/O while reset handling holds locks, matching the deadlock-prone root cause.
